meta.title: Seizure/Epilepsy Risk Score (critically ill children)
meta.authors: Abend NS, Fung FW, Parikh DS, Ramos M, Xiao R, Topjian AA
meta.outcome: Subsequent seizure or epilepsy diagnosis after acute symptomatic seizures in the PICU, from four clinical and continuous-EEG items.
meta.clinical_utility: Early risk stratification after acute symptomatic seizures in the PICU, to guide counselling and follow-up intensity. Not validated; not a basis for ASM decisions on its own.
meta.cff_info:
What this shows. The Seizure/Epilepsy Risk Score estimates the chance that a critically ill child with acute symptomatic seizures or acute encephalopathy is later diagnosed with seizures or epilepsy after hospital discharge (Abend et al., Epilepsia 2026).

How it is scored. One point each for developmental delay/intellectual disability, clinical seizures or status epilepticus before CEEG, electrographic seizures or status epilepticus during CEEG, and epileptiform discharges during CEEG (total 0–4). Each total maps to the observed proportion of children with a subsequent seizure/epilepsy diagnosis: 13% (score 0), 71% (1), 79% (2), 96% (3), 86% (4). Score 4 is based on only 7 children, which is why it sits below score 3; read it together with its wide confidence interval.

Cohort. Single-centre prospective cohort (Children's Hospital of Philadelphia PICU, 2017–2020): children older than 30 days with acute encephalopathy undergoing clinically indicated CEEG, without pre-existing epilepsy, who survived to discharge and had neurology follow-up (n=365 of 590 survivors). Median follow-up to the latest visit 1021 days. Overall, 64% had a subsequent seizure/epilepsy diagnosis; cumulative incidence was 27% at 30 days, 46% at 90 days, 61% at 1 year and 67% at 2 years.

Performance and limits. AUC 0.81 (95% CI 0.76–0.85) in the derivation cohort itself; the score has not been internally or externally validated. A score ≥1 had sensitivity 96%, specificity 53%, PPV 79% and NPV 88%. The outcome was an ICD-10 seizure/epilepsy code (R56/G40) at follow-up, not a chart-confirmed unprovoked seizure, and children with follow-up were enriched for in-hospital seizures, so absolute risks are probably overestimated. Risks are over the whole follow-up, not a fixed horizon.

Not treatment advice. Children discharged on antiseizure medication had a similar risk to those discharged without it after propensity adjustment (IPTW OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.61–1.72). The score informs counselling and follow-up intensity; it does not show that continuing ASM prevents seizures.

predictors.name: Developmental delay / intellectual disability
predictors.assess: Prior medical history of developmental delay or intellectual disability, present before the admission.

predictors.name: Clinical seizures or status epilepticus before CEEG
predictors.assess: Clinically evident seizures, or clinical status epilepticus, during the acute illness before continuous EEG monitoring was started.

predictors.name: Electrographic seizures or status epilepticus on CEEG
predictors.assess: Electrographic seizure = abnormal paroxysmal event distinct from the background, lasting >10 s, with a plausible field and evolution in morphology, frequency or amplitude. Electrographic status epilepticus = a single seizure ≥30 min, or seizures totalling >30 min in any 1-hour period (≥50% burden). Clinical and subclinical events both count.

predictors.name: Epileptiform discharges on CEEG
predictors.assess: Any of: sporadic interictal epileptiform discharges, lateralized periodic discharges (LPDs), generalized periodic discharges (GPDs) or lateralized rhythmic delta activity (LRDA), per the ACNS critical-care EEG terminology.

model.panel_title: Risk of a subsequent seizure or epilepsy diagnosis

rows.label: Score 0: 13% (10/80) had a subsequent seizure/epilepsy diagnosis
Score 1: 71% (87/123) had a subsequent seizure/epilepsy diagnosis
Score 2: 79% (81/103) had a subsequent seizure/epilepsy diagnosis
Score 3: 96% (50/52) had a subsequent seizure/epilepsy diagnosis
Score 4: 86% (6/7) had a subsequent seizure/epilepsy diagnosis — very small group, estimate unstable

model.note: Observed proportions in one derivation cohort (n=365), not validated. The outcome is an ICD-10 seizure/epilepsy code during follow-up (median ≈2.8 years), not a fixed horizon, and follow-up was enriched for higher-risk children, so risks are probably overestimated. Score 4 rests on 7 children. Not a basis for starting or stopping ASM on its own.
model.viz_info: Each of the four items adds one point; the waterfall shows the build-up from a child with none of them (13% observed risk). In the donut the grey wedge is that baseline risk and the coloured wedges share the rise above it; the centre is the observed proportion with a subsequent seizure/epilepsy diagnosis for the total score. The items are not strictly additive: the published risk for score 4 (86%, 7 children) is below score 3 (96%).
model.ci_note: 95% CIs are Wilson intervals calculated by predictepilepsy from the counts in Table 3 (the paper shows them only as error bars in Figure 4).

provenance.source: Abend et al., Epilepsia 2026 (doi 10.1002/epi.70452, PMID 42631926). Score items from Methods 2.5 and the Table 3 footnote; events/patients per score from Table 3 and Results 3.3; cohort figures from Results 3.2 and Table 1; AUC and threshold performance from Results 3.3; IPTW ASM result from Results 3.4.
provenance.notes: pct = events/n per score from Table 3, rounded to whole % as printed (13/71/79/96/86). CIs derived (Wilson, z=1.96) by 3_assemble/build_abend_asys_peds.py, not from the paper. Non-monotonic at score 4 (6/7) is reported as published; scores were not merged. The multivariable model (Table 2) is not implemented: no intercept is reported and it includes inpatient ASM administration. Deployed 2026-09-22 on the author's instruction; the per-score counts are asserted against Table 3 in the build script, but a row-by-row human comparison with the paper is still pending. Set review_status to human_reviewed after a person has done it.
